note: Claims Vasari's 1550 Lives both named the Renaissance and invented a murder its subjects could not have committed. Verified by renaissance-art coreSummary: "Giorgio Vasari's Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors, and Architects claims Andrea del Castagno killed fellow painter Domenico Veneziano ... Castagno actually died of plague in August 1457, nearly four years before Veneziano's recorded death in May 1461" -- i.e. Castagno was dead before Veneziano, making the murder impossible, and the same book's preface is the one that coined rinascita, the root of "Renaissance."
